'''Patricia A. Burrowes Gomez''' (born 1961) is an American [[herpetologist]]. She is a retired professor of biology from the [[University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus]] where she served as [[principal investigator]] of the Amphibian Disease Ecology Lab. Burrowes specializes in changes in amphibian population dynamics as a response to stressors of the Anthropocene, especially emergent infectious diseases. She is now an adjunct researcher at the National Museum of Natural History, CSIC, Madrid, Spain.

== Early life and education ==
Burrowes was born in 1961. In 1986, during her graduate studies, Burrowes and her doctoral advisor [[William E. Duellman]] collected specimens in Colombia and co-wrote ''A new species of marsupial frog (Hylidae: Gastrotheca) from the Andes of Southern Colombia''.<ref name="Beolens et al. 2013" /> She completed a M.A. in systematics and ecology in 1987 at [[University of Kansas]]. Her graduate thesis was titled ''An ecological study of a cloud forest herpetofauna in southern Columbia''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=An ecological study of a cloud forest herpetofauna in southern Colombia|date=1987|language=English|first=Patricia A|last=Burrowes|oclc=17615454}}</ref> Burrowes earned a Ph.D. in ecology and systematics in 1997 at University of Kansas. Her 1997 dissertation was titled ''The reproductive biology and population genetics of the cave-dwelling Puerto Rican frog, Eleutherodactylus cooki''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The reproductive biology and population genetics of the cave-dwelling Puerto Rican frog, Eleutherodactylus cooki|last=Burrowes, Patricia A.|oclc=37654794}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
In 1986, Burrowes began working with amphibians in Colombia, later she continued research on the amphibians of Puerto Rico but also collaborated in studies in other tropical countries. <ref name="Beolens et al. 2013" /> She was a professor in the biology department at the [[University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus]] where she served as [[principal investigator]] of the Amphibian Disease Ecology Lab.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://herplab.wixsite.com/burroweslab/people|title=People|website=burroweslab|language=en|access-date=2019-11-04}}</ref> <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://envsci.uprrp.edu/index.php?page=alias-2&hl=es_ES|title=EnvSci-UPRRP - Facultad del Programa Graduado|website=envsci.uprrp.edu|access-date=2019-11-04|archive-date=2021-01-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115183405/http://envsci.uprrp.edu/index.php?page=alias-2&hl=es_ES|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2019, Burrowes as part of a team of researchers published a study in [[Science (journal)|''Science'']] about a [[mycosis]] causing a dramatic population decrease in at least 501 species of amphibians.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/ciencia/ciencia/nota/unaprofesorayvariosestudiantesdelauprenriopiedrasparticipanenunainvestigaciondeimpactoglobal-2486008/|title=Una profesora y varios estudiantes de la UPR en Río Piedras participan en una investigación de impacto global|date=2019-04-03|website=El Nuevo Dia|language=es-pr|access-date=2019-11-05}}</ref>
